public_supplier_section:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$(V,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_V)$ and $(H,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_H)$ be
complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-inner-product-space]]) and let $i:V\to H$ be a linear map with dense
image.

**Symmetric forms.** A *sesquilinear form on $V$* is a map
$a:V\times V\to\mathbb C$ that is linear in its first argument and
conjugate-linear in its second; it is *symmetric* if
$a(u,v)=\overline{a(v,u)}$ for all $u,v\in V$, in which case $a(u,u)\in\mathbb R$
and $\operatorname{Re}a(u,v)=\operatorname{Re}\overline{a(v,u)}$.

**Bounded and semibounded.** Such a form is *bounded* if there is $C>0$ with
$|a(u,v)|\le C\|u\|_V\|v\|_V$ for all $u,v\in V$, and *semibounded below with
bound $M\ge0$* if $a(u,u)\ge-M\|i(u)\|_H^2$ for every $u\in V$.

**Form seminorm and closedness.** Let $M\ge0$ be a bound as above and define the
*form seminorm*
$$\|u\|_{a,M}:=\Bigl(\operatorname{Re}a(u,u)+(M+1)\|i(u)\|_H^2\Bigr)^{1/2}\qquad(u\in V).$$
It is a seminorm because $a(u,v)+(M+1)\langle i(u),i(v)\rangle_H$ is a positive semidefinite Hermitian form; its Cauchy–Schwarz inequality follows by expanding its value on $u+tv$ and minimizing over the scalar $t$, and gives the triangle inequality. It need not separate points for a general dense-image map $i$. The form $a$ is *closed* if there are such an $M$ and constants $c,C>0$ with
$c\|u\|_V\le\|u\|_{a,M}\le C\|u\|_V$ for every $u\in V$; then
the form seminorm is a norm, and $(V,\|\cdot\|_{a,M})$ is complete because $V$ is. If $i$ is injective, it is already a norm before closedness, since its square is at least $\|i(u)\|_H^2$.

**Associated operator.** With $a$ and $i$ as above, define
$$D(A):=\Bigl\{u\in V:\ \text{there is }f\in H\text{ with }a(u,v)=\langle f,i(v)\rangle_H\text{ for every }v\in V\Bigr\},\qquad Au:=f .$$
The element $f$ is unique when it exists, because two candidates differ by an
element of $H$ orthogonal to the dense subspace $i(V)$, hence coincide;
$A$ is called the *operator associated with $a$*. This definition asserts
neither that $A$ is densely defined, nor that $A$ is symmetric, nor that $A$ is
self-adjoint or bounded below; the specific closed semibounded form of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]] establishes those
properties for its own associated operator by a direct computation. When $V$
is a subspace of $H$ and $i$ is the inclusion, $\|i(u)\|_H$ is written
$\|u\|_H$ and the pairing $\langle f,i(v)\rangle_H$ is written
$\langle f,v\rangle$.

public_supplier_section:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Write
$L^2=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ for the complex Hilbert space of Lebesgue
(equivalence classes of) square-integrable functions with inner product
$\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f\overline g$ linear in the first
argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]]), and write $L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
for the same construction over the product with Lebesgue measure.

**Kernel data.** Let $k\in L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$.

**Domain and action.** For $f\in L^2$ say that the integral defining $T_kf$
*exists at* $x\in\mathbb R^3$ if the function
$y\mapsto k(x,y)f(y)$ lies in $L^1(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, and at such points
put
$$(T_kf)(x):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}k(x,y)f(y)\,dy .$$
Define
$$D(T_k):=\Bigl\{f\in L^2:\ x\mapsto(T_kf)(x)\ \text{exists for almost every }x\text{ and agrees a.e. with a class in }L^2\Bigr\},$$
and for $f\in D(T_k)$ let $T_kf$ denote that class. The assignment
$f\mapsto T_kf$ is called the *$L^2$-kernel operator with kernel $k$*.

**Hilbert-Schmidt operators.** A linear operator $T$ on $L^2$ is called a
*Hilbert-Schmidt operator* if there is
$k\in L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ with $D(T)=D(T_k)$ and
$T=T_k$; such a $k$ is called an *$L^2$ kernel* of $T$.

This definition asserts nothing about whether $D(T_k)$ is all of $L^2$,
whether $T_k$ is bounded, or whether $T_k$ is compact; those properties are
proved in [[lem-nrqm-coulomb-ltwo-kernel-operators-bounded-and-compact]]. A
finite product kernel $\sum_{i=1}^nf_i(x)\overline{g_i(y)}$ with
$f_i,g_i\in L^2$ is also a class in $L^2(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$,
as the same lemma records, so $T_k$ is defined for it whenever that membership
is used.

public_supplier_section:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) for a declared system, in the state, sharp-observable and evolution readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The readings below are the reading of clause (iv) of P4 for the page's models; clause (iv) records that a prescribed time-dependent family is **a different model assumption** from the autonomous one, and clause (b) below adopts it.

**(b) Prescribed energy family.** As an additional model assumption of the pair, fix a nonempty compact interval $I=[a,b]\subset\mathbb R$ of physical times (seconds), the declared state space $\mathfrak H$ of the system, a value $\hbar>0$ of the reduced Planck constant as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and a **prescribed family** $t\mapsto H(t)$ of self-adjoint operators on $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) in one of the following three **regularity classes**, whose hypotheses are part of the model declaration:

- **(i) Bounded norm-continuous class.** $D(H(t))=\mathfrak H$ for every $t$; each $H(t)\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is self-adjoint ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]); $t\mapsto H(t)$ is norm-continuous on $I$ ([[def-operator-norm]]); and $K:=\sup_{t\in I}\|H(t)\|/\hbar<\infty$.
- **(ii) Bounded-control class.** $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$, where $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(H_{0})\subseteq\mathfrak H$ and $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $\|V(t)\|=v(t)$, $v:=\sup_{t\in I}v(t)<\infty$.
- **(iii) Common-domain class.** There is a dense linear subspace $Y\subseteq\mathfrak H$ that is itself a Hilbert space continuously embedded in $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-hilbert-space]], for instance $Y=D(H_{0})$ with the graph norm of a self-adjoint $H_{0}$), with $D(H(t))=Y$ for every $t$, each $H(t)$ self-adjoint as an operator on $\mathfrak H$, and $t\mapsto H(t)$ of class $C^{1}(I;\mathcal B(Y,\mathfrak H))$.

The family, its class and its data are **prescribed**: no field equation, source model, back-reaction or feedback of the system on the source is assumed, and no claim is made that any laboratory arrangement realizes the family. The family is coupled to the system through the material hypotheses of the page or of the item that declares a specific model (for instance a magnetic-moment or electric-dipole coupling, or the external-source Coulomb family of the page's adiabatic models); the reading of $H(t)$ as the energy of the declared system is a model assumption.

**(c) The model's evolution.** The **driven model** declares that the time evolution of the system between times $s,t\in I$ is carried by a family $U(t,s)$ of unitary operators on $\mathfrak H$ with
$$U(s,s)=I,\qquad U(t,r)=U(t,s)U(s,r)\quad(r,s,t\in I),\qquad U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t),$$
jointly strongly continuous in $(t,s)$, solving the time-dependent Schroedinger equation on $I$ in the sense of the class:
in class (i) $U$ is the unique norm-continuous solution of $i\hbar\partial_tU(t,s)=H(t)U(t,s)$ with $U(s,s)=I$ constructed by the Dyson series of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]] (whose hypothesis is exactly the norm-continuity of the bounded self-adjoint family);
in class (ii) $U$ is the mild propagator constructed in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]], satisfying $U(t,s)\psi=E(t-s)\psi-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_s^tE(t-r)V(r)U(r,s)\psi\,dr$ for every $\psi\in\mathfrak H$, with $E(u)=e^{-iuH_{0}/\hbar}$ the autonomous flow of clause (b) of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]];
in class (iii) $U$ is the strong propagator of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-common-domain-nonautonomous-evolution]] with physical generator $A=H/\hbar$, preserving $Y$, for which $t\mapsto U(t,s)y$ is $C^1$ in $\mathfrak H$ with $i\hbar\partial_tU(t,s)y=H(t)U(t,s)y$ for every $y\in Y$.
In each class the cited item is what makes the declaration well posed: it constructs the family and proves uniqueness under the class hypotheses. The model asserts nothing beyond those hypotheses; in particular it asserts no invariant domain and no strong equation for $H_{0}$-domain vectors in class (ii), and no common domain in classes (i) and (ii).

**(d) State and outcome readings.** The **evolved preparation** at time $t$ of a preparation $\rho$ specified at time $s$ is $\rho(t):=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$; it is a preparation of the model in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] for every $t$, by unitarity of $U(t,s)$ and [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]. A pure preparation $[\psi(s)]$ evolves to the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$ with $\psi(t):=U(t,s)\psi(s)\ne0$. The **outcome law at time $t$** of an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]) in that preparation is $\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}$, the reading of P2; the definition records the timing convention once and asserts nothing about how or when a record is produced.

**(e) Energy-basis amplitudes and level populations.** In class (ii), let $(\varphi_{j})_{j\in J}$ be an orthonormal family in $D(H_{0})$ with $H_{0}\varphi_{j}=E_{j}\varphi_{j}$ and $E_{j}\in\mathbb R$ (a complete orthonormal family of eigenvectors is not assumed here). For $s\le t$ and labels $i,j$ the **transition amplitude from $i$ at time $s$ to $j$ at time $t$** is the scalar
$$A_{ji}(t,s):=e^{iE_{j}(t-s)/\hbar}\,\bigl\langle U(t,s)\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle ,$$
and the **transition probability** is $p_{ji}(t,s):=|A_{ji}(t,s)|^{2}$. If additionally $E_{j}$ is a simple eigenvalue of $H_{0}$ with spectral projection $P_{j}=E_{H_{0}}(\{E_{j}\})$ onto $\mathbb C\varphi_{j}$, then the definition *states*, as the reading of P2, the identity
$$p_{ji}(t,s)=\mu^{H_{0}}_{\psi(t)}(\{E_{j}\})=\|E_{H_{0}}(\{E_{j}\})\psi(t)\|^{2},\qquad \psi(t)=U(t,s)\varphi_{i},$$
which follows from the rank-one form of $P_{j}$ and the normalization $\|\varphi_{j}\|=1$; $p_{ji}$ is the reading of the outcome probability of the value $E_{j}$ of the assigned energy observable $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$ in the evolved preparation, and it is a property of the declared model, not a measured frequency.

**(f) Declared two-level drive models.** Let $(\sigma_{x},\sigma_{y},\sigma_{z})$ be the Pauli matrices of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e) acting on $\mathbb C^{2}$ in the orthonormal basis $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ ([[def-inner-product-space]]), let $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega\in\mathbb R$, and put $H_{0}:=\frac{\hbar}{2}\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}$ (class (i) with $I$ any compact interval). The **circular two-level drive model** is the class-(i) family
$$H_{\mathrm c}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\bigl(\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}+\sin(\omega t)\sigma_{y}\bigr)\Bigr),$$
and the **linear two-level drive model** is the class-(i) family
$$H_{\mathrm l}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}\bigr).$$
The dimensionless numbers $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega$ are read as angular frequencies in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; $\omega_{0}$ is the **splitting frequency** of the model (the level gap is $\hbar|\omega_{0}|$), $\omega$ the **drive frequency**, $\Omega_{1}$ the **transverse coupling**, and $\Delta:=\omega_{0}-\omega$ the **detuning**. Populations of the level pair are the diagonal entries $\langle P_{\bullet}\psi,\psi\rangle$ of the orthogonal projections $P_{\uparrow},P_{\downarrow}$ onto $\mathbb Ce_{\uparrow},\mathbb Ce_{\downarrow}$ in the evolved vector $\psi(t)$. The two families are model data: no identification with a laboratory spin, molecule or field, and no relation of $\Omega_{1}$ to a field amplitude, is asserted; such an identification is a tested identification in the sense of P7.

**(g) Status and scope.** Clauses (b), (c), (f) are adopted model assumptions and readings; the existence and uniqueness of the propagator in each class is cited mathematics, not a consequence of P1, P2 or P4. The model asserts no open-system or environment coupling, no non-unitary reduced dynamics, no measurement or apparatus model, no thermalization or equilibration, no long-time limit and no empirical record; the identification of the family's parameters with laboratory fields and of the system with a laboratory sample is made, if at all, only in separately declared models with their own uncertainty.

public_supplier_section:
**(a) Setting.** Adopt the framework data and the declared driven model of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] in the **bounded-control class** of its clause (b)(ii): $\mathfrak H$ is the model's state space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint on its exact dense domain $D(H_{0})$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $v=\sup_{t\in I}\|V(t)\|<\infty$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]), $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$ on $D(H_{0})$, and $U(t,s)$ is the mild propagator of clause (c)(ii) constructed in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]]. The readings of P1 and P2 are those of [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]; all times lie in $I$ and are read in seconds as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) The free-flow factor.** The **free-flow factor** of the model is the autonomous flow of the unperturbed part,
$$E(t):=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the reading of clause (b) of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] applied to the assigned energy observable $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$; it is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group on all real arguments. This auxiliary group supplies $E(-t)$ and $E(t-s)$ even when those arguments lie outside $I$; the physical driven evaluation times $s,t$ remain in $I$. The **interaction-picture control** is the family $V_{I}:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$,
$$V_{I}(t):=E(-t)V(t)E(t),$$
which is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $\|V_{I}(t)\|=\|V(t)\|\le v$. The **interaction propagator** is
$$U_{I}(t,s):=E(-t)U(t,s)E(s)\qquad(s,t\in I),$$
and the model's clause (c)(ii) supplies, as the cited theorem proves, the decomposition
$$U(t,s)=E(t)U_{I}(t,s)E(-s).$$
The interaction propagator is unitary, jointly strongly continuous, satisfies $U_{I}(s,s)=I$ and the cocycle $U_{I}(t,r)=U_{I}(t,s)U_{I}(s,r)$, and its first-endpoint map is strongly differentiable with
$$i\hbar\,\partial_{t}U_{I}(t,s)\psi=V_{I}(t)U_{I}(t,s)\psi\qquad(\psi\in\mathfrak H),$$
all as supplied by [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]]; these are readings of that theorem in the model's vocabulary, not new assumptions.

**(c) Interaction states and preparations.** For a Schroedinger-picture state vector $\psi(t)=U(t,s)\psi(s)$ the **interaction-picture state** is
$$\psi_{I}(t):=E(-t)\psi(t),\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad\psi_{I}(t)=U_{I}(t,s)\psi_{I}(s),$$
and for a preparation $\rho$ with $\rho(t)=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$ the **interaction-picture preparation** is
$$\rho_{I}(t):=E(-t)\rho(t)E(t),$$
which is again a preparation of the model by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]; for a pure preparation $[\psi(s)]$, $[\psi_{I}(t)]$ is pure. The map $\psi(t)\mapsto\psi_{I}(t)$ is unitary at every $t$, so $\|\psi_{I}(t)\|=\|\psi(t)\|$.

**(d) The two pictures assign the same outcome laws.** Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ bounded and let $A_{I}(t):=E(-t)AE(t)$ be its interaction-picture representative, which is again a bounded self-adjoint observable with $E_{A_{I}(t)}(B)=E(-t)E_{A}(B)E(t)$ for every Borel set $B$ by clause (d) of [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] applied to the flow $E$ of the self-adjoint $T=-H_{0}/\hbar$. Then for every preparation $\rho$ specified at $s$ and every $t\in I$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A_{I}(t)}_{\rho_{I}(t)}(B)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
because $\rho(t)=E(t)\rho_{I}(t)E(-t)$ and $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(E(t)\rho_{I}E(-t)E_{A}(B)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho_{I}E(-t)E_{A}(B)E(t)\bigr)$ by cyclicity of the trace; equivalently, for a pure preparation, $\|E_{A}(B)\psi(t)\|=\|E_{A_{I}(t)}(B)\psi_{I}(t)\|$. This identity is the precise sense in which the two pictures are two bookkeeping devices for the same model; it is a reading of P2 together with the cited mathematics, not a claim about apparatuses.

**(e) Energy-basis transition amplitudes.** Let $\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\in D(H_{0})$ be unit eigenvectors, $H_{0}\varphi_{a}=E_{a}\varphi_{a}$, $H_{0}\varphi_{b}=E_{b}\varphi_{b}$, and let $A_{ba}(t,s)$ and $p_{ba}(t,s)$ be the transition amplitude and probability of clause (e) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]]. Then
$$A_{ba}(t,s)=e^{is(E_{a}-E_{b})/\hbar}\bigl\langle U_{I}(t,s)\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\bigr\rangle ,\qquad\text{hence}\qquad p_{ba}(t,s)=\bigl|\bigl\langle U_{I}(t,s)\varphi_{a},\varphi_{b}\bigr\rangle\bigr|^{2},$$
by the decomposition of clause (b) and $E(-s)\varphi_{a}=e^{isE_{a}/\hbar}\varphi_{a}$, $\langle E(t)\chi,\varphi_{b}\rangle=e^{-itE_{b}/\hbar}\langle\chi,\varphi_{b}\rangle$; the phases are of modulus one ([[def-inner-product-space]]). The transition probability is therefore computable in either picture, and the definition records this as the reading used by the page's amplitude theorem; no measurement frequency or rate is defined.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (b)-(e) are readings of the declared driven model, of clauses (b)-(e) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]], and of P1 and P2, in the vocabulary of the cited mathematics. The interaction picture is a change of description of the same model: it adds no assumption, no physical process, no measurement and no empirical claim, and it asserts nothing about detectors, records or the laboratory realization of the model.

public_supplier_section:
**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1) and the
identical-particle and spin postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] (P6), read with the state
space vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and the
quantities and units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis of the cited tensor construction.

**(b) Declared species and sector.** A **declared species sector** of the model
consists of: a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$, the
**one-particle space** of the species, as assigned in P1; a mass parameter
$m>0$ in kg; a spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and the
internal factor $V_{s}=\mathbb C^{2s+1}$ of P6 clause (ii), with the
**orbital factor** $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ the factor carrying no internal degree of
freedom when the one-particle space is given as a completed product
$H_{\mathrm{sp}}\widehat\otimes V_{s}$; for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] the one-particle space
is $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$, whose spin components are the
internal factor of P6 clause (ii) in the reading of that definition; a
**statistics choice**
$\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, where $+$ declares the species **bosonic** and $-$
declares it **fermionic**; and, for a charged species, a charge parameter
$q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs. The parameters and the statistics choice are
empirical model assignments with their uncertainties, in the sense of P6
clause (iii); no value and no statistics choice is derived by this definition.

**(c) The $n$-particle sector.** Fix $n\ge1$. The **labelled $n$-particle
space** of the species is the $n$-fold completed tensor power
$H^{\otimes n}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), whose
tensor factors are mathematical labels and not observable particle
identities, equipped with the permutation unitaries $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$
and the sector projections $P_\sigma^{(n)}$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]), where
$P_+^{(n)}$ is the symmetrizing projection and $P_-^{(n)}$ the alternating
projection. The **$n$-particle sector space** of the declared species is
$$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\ \subseteq\ H^{\otimes n},$$
a closed linear subspace carrying the inner product of $H^{\otimes n}$; on it
every permutation acts by the scalar
$$U_\pi|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)\, \mathrm{id}_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma},\qquad \operatorname{sgn}_+(\pi)=1,\quad \operatorname{sgn}_-(\pi)=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi),$$
by clause (c) of the cited permutation lemma. For $n=1$ one has
$\mathfrak H_1^+=\mathfrak H_1^-=H$.

**(d) Declared sector preparations.** A **declared sector preparation** of $n$
particles of the species is a state of the framework on the sector space,
that is a density operator
$$\rho\in D(\mathfrak H_n^\sigma)$$
in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and
clause (a) of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], read as the
state assigned to the preparation by P1 clause (iii). A **pure sector
preparation** is a pure state, i.e. the rank-one operator of a unit ray of
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$; a statistical mixture of sector preparations is a
convex combination. The sector is part of the declaration of the species: a
model that declares one statistics choice does not switch it within the same
declaration. When a sector preparation is paired with an operator or a
spectral projection on the labelled space, use its **canonical zero extension**
$\widetilde\rho:=j\rho j^*$, where $j:\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\hookrightarrow
H^{\otimes n}$ is the isometric inclusion and $j^*$ is the orthogonal
projection viewed as a map into the sector. This extension is a density
operator on the labelled space: by clause (a) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]],
$\rho=\sum_kw_kT_{u_k,u_k}$ in trace norm for an orthonormal family in the
sector and nonnegative weights summing to one. The family $(ju_k)$ is
orthonormal in the labelled space, so the same clause gives the density
$\sum_kw_kT_{ju_k,ju_k}$ there; its action is $j\rho j^*$, since both agree on
the sector and vanish on its orthogonal complement. If the sector is zero,
there is no density preparation of trace one and this convention is vacuous.

**(e) Sector quantities.** Let $A$ be a linear operator on the labelled space
$H^{\otimes n}$ with domain $D(A)$. The model reads $A$ as a **quantity of the
declared sector** only when $A$ **preserves the sector**,
$$P_\sigma^{(n)}D(A)\subseteq D(A),\qquad A\bigl(D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\bigr)\subseteq \mathfrak H_n^\sigma,$$
in which case the **sector restriction** $A_\sigma:=A|_{\mathfrak H_n^\sigma}$
with domain $D(A)\cap\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ is part of the declaration and is
the quantity actually read on sector preparations; For any bounded $A$, commutation with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$ implies sector
preservation; for bounded self-adjoint $A$ the converse also holds. Indeed,
if such an $A$ preserves the sector, $y$ in its orthogonal complement and
$x$ in the sector satisfy $\langle Ay,x\rangle=\langle y,Ax\rangle=0$,
so the complement is invariant as well; splitting each vector into its two
orthogonal components gives $AP_\sigma^{(n)}=P_\sigma^{(n)}A$. For an arbitrary
bounded operator, invariance alone need not preserve the complement and is
not asserted equivalent to commutation. An
operator that does not preserve the sector is not read on the sector; in
particular no quantity of a single labelled factor is assumed to define a
quantity of the sector unless it preserves it. If $A_\sigma$ is self-adjoint,
its outcome law in a sector preparation is the law of

consists of:

1. a nonzero **propagation label** $k_{0}\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$, read
   in $\mathrm m^{-1}$ in a declared inertial chart, which is a parameter of the
   model and not a state;
2. a declared **transverse frame**, that is an orthonormal pair $(v_{1},v_{2})$
   in the euclidean space $\mathbb C^{3}$ with $\langle v_{i},v_{j}\rangle=\delta_{ij}$
   and $k_{0}\cdot v_{1}=k_{0}\cdot v_{2}=0$;
3. the **polarisation space** $V:=\mathbb Cv_{1}\oplus\mathbb Cv_{2}$ with the
   restricted Hermitian inner product and the orthonormal basis
   $(e_{1},e_{2}):=(v_{1},v_{2})$.

The model's **state space** is $D(V)$, the set of density operators of $V$; the
**pure preparations** of the model are the unit rays $[\psi]$ of $V$, that is
the preparations assigned the pure state $\widehat\rho(\psi)$ of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], and a **mixed
preparation** is a statistical mixture of preparations in the sense of P1. The
map $\theta\mapsto\psi_{\theta}:=\cos\theta\,e_{1}+\sin\theta\,e_{2}$ assigns
to each angle $\theta\in\mathbb R$ a distinguished pure preparation, the
**linear polarisation preparation at angle $\theta$** in the declared
transverse frame.

**(c) Declared polarisation analyser.** For each angle $\theta\in\mathbb R$ the
**declared polarisation analyser at angle $\theta$** is the declared ideal
sharp measurement of clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] with
two outcomes labelled $+1$ and $-1$ and outcome structure
$$(P_{\theta},\,P_{\theta}^{\perp}),\qquad P_{\theta}x=\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle e_{\theta},\quad e_{\theta}:=\cos\theta\,e_{1}+\sin\theta\,e_{2},\qquad P_{\theta}^{\perp}:=I-P_{\theta},$$
whose projections $P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are those of
[[lem-nrqm-photons-analyzer-projections-and-overlaps]]. The **outcome law** of
the analyser in a preparation $\rho$ is the reading of P2 for the projections
of the outcome structure, and the labels are dimensionless with the reading
"$+1$: transmitted", "$-1$: blocked". Where a conditional post-measurement
state is used, it is the Lueders update of clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]; the
framework does not assert that a laboratory absorber leaves an outgoing
one-photon polarisation state, and the absorption outcome is used only through
its discarded-outcome law unless a separate instrument is declared (clause (v)
of P3).

**(d) Frame covariance and angle labels.** For another complex orthonormal transverse pair $(e_1',e_2')$, let $U:V\to V$ be the unitary map with $Ue_i=e_i'$, explicitly $Ux=\sum_i\langle x,e_i\rangle e_i'$. with a definite mode label. It is a finite-dimensional internal-factor model
in the sense of P1 and P6: its state space is $D(V)$, its preparations are
rays, and its analyser is a declared ideal sharp measurement. It contains no
position observable, no momentum observable, no spatial wave function and no
localisation claim, and it is not the massive one-particle model of P5 with
$m=0$ and is not obtained from that model by a mass-to-zero limit; no such
limit is used or claimed. The mode label $k_{0}$ is not a
normalisable state of any sector of the framework, and a plane wave is not
introduced as a state. Whether a laboratory polariser and source realize this
declared model, with what efficiency, loss and background, is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7, not a consequence of this
definition.

its scope; they add no assumption beyond the cited postulates and the cited
finite-dimensional mathematics. The mathematical properties of the projections
are the content of
[[lem-nrqm-photons-analyzer-projections-and-overlaps]]; the conditional outcome law of the declared analyser is proved on this page. No empirical claim is made here.

**(b) Radiation one-particle space and sectors.** The **transverse one-particle
space** of the radiation sector is
$$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3}):\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for almost every }k\Bigr\}$$
with the restricted $L^{2}$ inner product, a separable complex Hilbert space
([[def-hilbert-space]]); its elements are read as **one-photon wave-packet
vectors**. For $n\ge1$ the **$n$-photon sector** is
$\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}=\operatorname{ran}P_{+}^{(n)}\subseteq\mathfrak h^{\otimes n}$
and the **radiation state space** is the bosonic Fock space
$F(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}$, whose sector projections
are $\Pi_n$ and whose vacuum is $\Omega=\iota_0(1)$
([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]],
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]]). A **declared
radiation preparation** is a state $\rho\in D(F(\mathfrak h))$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]; a **declared one-photon
preparation** is a preparation whose state is supported in the one-photon
sector, and for a unit $f\in\mathfrak h$ the ray of $\iota_{1}(f)$ is the
one-photon preparation **of wave-packet vector $f$**.

**(c) Modes.** A **mode** of the radiation sector is a nonzero class
$\varphi\in\mathfrak h$ considered up to phase, equivalently the rank-one
orthogonal projection onto $\mathbb C\varphi$; a **declared mode family** is a
finite or countable orthonormal family $(\varphi_{j})$ of $\mathfrak h$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). For
a unit mode vector $\varphi$ and $z\in\mathbb C$ the vector
$$U_\varphi\psi_z,\qquad \psi_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}e_n,$$
is the **mode-coherent preparation vector of label $z$**, and $U_\varphi e_n$
is the **$n$-quanta mode vector**; these are the readings of the transferred
vectors of [[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]]. A mode vector is a
normalisable wave packet; the sharp-mode label $k$ of the propagation-mode
idealisation is a spectral parameter and is not a state of $\mathfrak h$
([[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]]
clause (c)).

**(d) Assigned observables.** The framework assigns to the radiation sector:

1. the **total number observable** $(N,1)$, the self-adjoint number operator of
   [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]], with domain
   $D(N)=\{\psi:\sum_nn^{2}\|\psi_n\|^{2}<\infty\}$ and read in the
   dimensionless unit $1$ of counted quanta;
2. the **free-field energy observable** $(H_f,\mathrm J)$, the operator
   $H_f=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_{n}$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$ and
   $T_{n}\psi=\varepsilon_{n}\psi$, of
   [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]],
   read in joules; its one-particle restriction is the energy multiplier
   $M_{\hbar c|k|}^{\mathfrak h}$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]];

Its Fock domain is
   $$D(P_j)=\{\psi:\psi_n\in D(P_{j,n})\text{ for every }n,\ \sum_n\|P_{j,n}\psi_n\|^2<\infty\}.$$
   This is the domain of the sum, without an extra requirement that each individual momentum summand be square integrable. Its spectral PVM is the sectorwise direct sum of the inverse-image indicator multipliers, including the atom at zero on the vacuum. The **one-photon momentum component** is its restriction to sector one, identified with $M_{\hbar k_j}^{\mathfrak h}$ of [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]]. The postulate assigns these mathematical operators their physical momentum meaning and units.

**(e) Reading of the mode assignments.** In the declared inertial chart the
assignments $\omega(k)=c|k|$ in $\mathrm s^{-1}$, $E(k)=\hbar\omega(k)$ in
$\mathrm J$ and $p(k)=\hbar k$ in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ of
clause (iii) of the radiation postulate are read through the spectral measures
of clause (d): for a one-photon preparation of unit wave-packet vector
$f\in\mathfrak h$, the **assigned frequency**, **energy** and
**momentum component** laws are the push-forwards of the measure
$\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k$ under $k\mapsto c|k|$,
$k\mapsto\hbar c|k|$ and $k\mapsto\hbar k_{j}$; these laws, and their finite means under the corresponding first-moment conditions, are proved on this page. Sharp
frequency, sharp energy and sharp momentum-component states are not vectors of
$\mathfrak h$; every unit one-photon vector in the corresponding multiplier domain has
finite strictly positive variance in that quantity (clause (d) of
[[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]]).
The push-forward laws themselves exist for every unit $f\in\mathfrak h$, without a moment-domain assumption; all their singleton probabilities vanish by the null level sets in the cited lemma, so they are non-Dirac laws even when finite means or variances do not exist. assert no detector model, no sampling model, no dynamics, no interaction with
matter, no spontaneous emission and no empirical result; the counting and detection vocabulary is fixed separately on this page. The
identification of a laboratory radiation field with a preparation of
$F(\mathfrak h)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7, and no
Lorentz transformation law for modes or their labels is adopted or claimed.

(a) A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). If $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ is a finite or countable orthonormal family, with $J$ a finite initial segment of the positive integers or all positive integers, and $w_n\ge0$ with $\sum_nw_n=1$, then the sum $\rho:=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ converges in trace norm to a density operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$. Conversely every density operator $\rho$ admits such an expansion whose weights are its positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity and whose vectors are orthonormal eigenvectors; distinct expansions of the same $\rho$ exist when a positive eigenspace has dimension at least two.

(b) Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then $\mu_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a well-defined probability measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ ([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]); it is given by the absolutely convergent series $\mu_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^2$ in every expansion of (a), and reduces to $\mu_\rho(B)=\|E(B)u\|^2$ for a pure density operator $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$.

(c) Assume in addition the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator with projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let $\psi\in H$ have $\|\psi\|=1$ and $\psi\in D(A)$. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^2 ,$$

where $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]); moreover $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean $\int\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}$ is finite. Recall that an endomorphism $F$ is an **effect** when $F\ge0$ and $I-F\ge0$, i.e. $0\le F\le I$ in the quadratic-form order ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]).

(a) *Definitions.* A finite POVM is a finite family $(F_a)_{a=1}^p$ of effects with $\sum_aF_a=I$. [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]]. Fix a unit

$\varphi^{\otimes n}:=\varphi\otimes\cdots\otimes\varphi\in H^{\otimes n}$ for

$$U_\varphi:F(\mathbb C)\to F(H),\qquad U_\varphi e_n:=(0,\dots,0,\varphi^{\otimes n},0,\dots)$$

is orthonormal in $F(H)$, and $U_\varphi$ is a linear isometry of

([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]],
[[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]],
[[def-bounded-linear-operator]]);

$$\Pi_nU_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi\Pi_n'\psi,\qquad \|U_\varphi\psi\|^{2}=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\psi_n|^{2}=\|\psi\|^{2},$$
where $\Pi_n'$ is the Fock sector projection of $F(\mathbb C)$; and for every
$\psi\in D(N')$ one has $U_\varphi\psi\in D(N)$ with
$$NU_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi N'\psi ;$$

(c) for every $\psi\in D(A_\pm(1))$ one has $U_\varphi\psi\in D(A_\pm(\varphi))$
and
$$A_\pm(\varphi)U_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi A_\pm(1)\psi ;$$

$U_\varphi\psi_z\in D(A_-(\varphi))$ and $A_-(\varphi)U_\varphi\psi_z=z\,U_\varphi\psi_z$;

[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]

$\varepsilon\varphi\in\mathfrak h$), one has
$$\langle H_fU_\varphi e_n,U_\varphi e_n\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle\qquad(n\in\mathbb N),$$

$$\|T_n\varphi^{\otimes n}\|^2=n\|\varepsilon\varphi\|^2+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^2.$$

$$\langle T_n\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle,\qquad \langle T_n^{2}\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon^{2}\varphi,\varphi\rangle+n(n-1)\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle^{2}.$$

Assume Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), carrying the actual hypotheses of the multiplier and Fock suppliers. Fix a positive real parameter $\hbar$ and let
$$G=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3),\qquad \mathfrak h=\{f\in G:k\cdot f(k)=0\text{ for a.e. }k\},\qquad \Pi(k)=I-|k|^{-2}kk^{\mathsf T}\ (k\ne0),\quad \Pi(0)=0.$$
Use the Hilbert tensor powers of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], the symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]], and the Fock space of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], with sectors $\mathfrak H_n=\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\subset\mathfrak h^{\otimes n}$ for $n\ge1$ and $\mathfrak H_0=\mathbb C$.

For $n\ge1$ there is a canonical isometric embedding
$$I_n:\mathfrak H_n\longrightarrow L_n:=L^2(\mathbb R^{3n};(\mathbb C^3)^{\otimes n}),$$
obtained by inclusion into $G^{\otimes n}$ followed by the iterated finite-component Euclidean product unitary of [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]. On elementary tensors before symmetrization that unitary sends $f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n$ to $(k_1,\ldots,k_n)\mapsto f_1(k_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n(k_n)$. Write $K_n=I_n\mathfrak H_n$, a closed subspace. For $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ put
$$p_{j,n}(k_1,\ldots,k_n)=\hbar\sum_{i=1}^n(k_i)_j,\qquad D(P_{j,n})=\{u\in\mathfrak H_n:p_{j,n}I_nu\in L_n\},\qquad P_{j,n}u=I_n^{-1}(p_{j,n}I_nu).$$
The displayed product always lies in $K_n$ whenever it lies in $L_n$, so this action is well-defined. Set $P_{j,0}=0$ on $\mathbb C$. Then:

**(a) Sector self-adjointness and spectral measure.** Every $P_{j,n}$ is densely defined and self-adjoint on its sector. For Borel $B\subset\mathbb R$, its regular spectral PVM is
$$E_{j,n}(B)u=I_n^{-1}(\mathbf1_{p_{j,n}^{-1}(B)}I_nu)\quad(n\ge1),\qquad E_{j,0}(B)=\mathbf1_B(0)I_{\mathbb C}.$$
In particular $D(P_{j,n})$ is exactly the square-integrability domain of the signed summed multiplier, without requiring the individual summands to be square integrable separately.

**(b) Total momentum.** On $F(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak H_n$ define
$$D(P_j)=\{\psi:\psi_n\in D(P_{j,n})\text{ for every }n,\ \sum_{n\ge0}\|P_{j,n}\psi_n\|^2<\infty\},\qquad (P_j\psi)_n=P_{j,n}\psi_n.$$
Then $P_j$ is densely defined and self-adjoint on precisely this domain. Equivalently its domain is given by
$$\sum_{n\ge1}\int_{\mathbb R^{3n}}|p_{j,n}(k)|^2\|I_n\psi_n(k)\|^2\,d^{3n}k<\infty.$$
Its regular spectral PVM is the sectorwise direct sum
$$E_j(B)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}E_{j,n}(B),\qquad P_j=\int_{\mathbb R}t\,dE_j(t).$$
For every $\psi\in F(\mathfrak h)$, without a domain assumption, its scalar spectral measure is
$$\langle E_j(B)\psi,\psi\rangle=\mathbf1_B(0)|\psi_0|^2+\sum_{n\ge1}\int_{p_{j,n}^{-1}(B)}\|I_n\psi_n(k)\|^2\,d^{3n}k.$$
Thus it is the sum of the sectorwise push-forward measures and the vacuum atom. The vacuum belongs to $D(P_j)$ and $P_j\Omega=0$. On the one-particle sector the operator is the restricted multiplier $f\mapsto\hbar k_jf$ on its maximal square-integrability domain.

These are mathematical operator/domain statements. They adopt no photon assignment, probability law, dispersion relation, dynamical law or relation between momentum, energy and number operators.

valid only for the declared finite-level model of this clause, the following
static electric-dipole coupling. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the
Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematical suppliers
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(i) Declared charged pair and relative coordinate.** Take the declared
two-body Coulomb model of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (d): two
distinguishable spinless particles with mass parameters $m_{1},m_{2}>0$ and
opposite charges $-q$ and $+q$, $q>0$ (coulombs), with the relative coordinate
$r=x_{1}-x_{2}$ and the centre-of-mass/relative unitary
$U_{\Phi}$. Work in the relative-coordinate factor $L^{2}(\mathbb
R^{3};\mathbb C)$ of that reading, with Coulomb mass parameter $m=\mu:=m_{1}m_{2}/(m_{1}+m_{2})$, and with units as in
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**(ii) Dipole operator.** Let $Q_{j}$, $j=1,2,3$, be the coordinate
multiplication operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with maximal
domains $D(Q_{j})=\{\psi:\xi_{j}\psi\in L^{2}\}$ of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-atomic-dipole-matrix-element-domain]] clause (a); they are
self-adjoint and proper densely defined. The model's **dipole operator** is
the triple
$$D_{j}:=-q\,Q_{j}\qquad(j=1,2,3),$$
because the dipole of charges $-q$ at $x_{1}$ and $+q$ at $x_{2}$ is
$-qx_{1}+qx_{2}=-qr$: it points from the negative to the positive charge,
opposite to the declared relative coordinate $r=x_{1}-x_{2}$. Each $D_{j}$ is
self-adjoint on $D(Q_{j})$ and has unit $\mathrm{C\,m}$. This is the dipole of
the declared pair in its relative-coordinate reading; no multipole expansion,
no field equation and no coupling to the centre-of-mass motion is assumed.

**(iii) Finite-level truncation.** Fix, as part of the model specification, a
**declared finite-dimensional subspace** $W\subseteq D(H_\kappa)\cap D(Q_{1})\cap D(Q_{2})\cap
D(Q_{3})$ of the relative-coordinate space with $D(H_\kappa)=H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and $\dim W=d<\infty$, together
with an orthonormal basis of $W$. The model declares the **compressed dipole
matrix** on $W$,
$$D^{W}_{j}:=\Pi_{W}D_{j}\big|_{W},$$
where $\Pi_{W}$ is the orthogonal projection onto $W$ and the restriction to
$W$ is read in the declared orthonormal basis; $D^{W}_{j}$ is the finite
Hermitian $d\times d$ matrix of the dipole component, with unit
$\mathrm{C\,m}$, and it is bounded with norm at most $\sup_{\psi\in
W,\|\psi\|=1}\|D_{j}\psi\|$. The truncation and the basis are model
assumptions: they are not derived from the Coulomb model, and they replace
the unbounded operator $D_{j}$ by its compression throughout this pair.

**(iv) Static uniform field and interaction operator.** The external datum is
a **uniform static electric field value** $\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\in\mathbb
R^{3}$, read in $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$; it is prescribed, and no Maxwell
equation, source model, propagation or back-reaction is assumed. The
**finite-level static Stark model** is the finite-dimensional operator on $W$
$$H_{S}(\mathbf E_{\rm ext}):=\Pi_{W}H_{\kappa}\big|_{W} -\sum_{j=1}^{3}E_{{\rm ext},j}\,D^{W}_{j},$$
where the energy-domain condition of (iii) makes the compression defined,
and $H_{\kappa}=C_{\mu}$ is the one-centre Coulomb energy operator with
mass parameter $m=\mu$ of the declared model, read on the relative-coordinate
factor through the angular/radial
identification used by the pair. The interaction term has unit
$\mathrm{C\,m\cdot V\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm J$ and is bounded Hermitian on $W$, so
$H_{S}(\mathbf E_{\rm ext})$ is a bounded Hermitian $d\times d$ matrix and

bounded perturbation; this identification of the matrix with the model's
energy on the truncated subspace is a model assumption.

**(v) Scope and explicit exclusion.** Clauses (i)-(iv) are adopted model
assumptions. They assert nothing about a laboratory atom, field or apparatus;
no measured Stark shift is claimed; no transition, absorption or emission
rate is defined; and no time dependence of the field is assumed. In
particular the postulate deliberately does **not** treat the uncompressed

perturbation of $H_{\kappa}$: the uncompressed term is an unbounded
multiplication operator, and the energy form of $H_{\kappa}$ plus that term
has no lower bound for a nonzero field, so the uncompressed static-field model
is outside the scope of every statement of this pair. Only the compressed

[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],

hypotheses of the cited Fock space mathematics ([[def-countable-choice]],

**(i) Fixed propagation-mode one-photon polarisation model.** For a declared
propagation mode, described by a nonzero wavevector label
$k_{0}\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ read in $\mathrm m^{-1}$ in a declared
inertial chart ([[def-nrqm-framework-inertial-frames]]), the model assigns a
two-dimensional complex internal space, the **transverse polarisation space**
of the mode: the complex span of an orthonormal pair $(v_{1},v_{2})$ of vectors
of $\mathbb C^{3}$ satisfying $k_{0}\cdot v_{1}=k_{0}\cdot v_{2}=0$, with the
standard Hermitian form. Unit rays of this space are the model's **one-photon
polarisation preparations** of the mode. This assignment is an idealised
manifestation of the abstract Born/state framework on a finite-dimensional
internal factor; it is not a spatial wave function of a massive particle, not a
model of a photon position, and not the massive one-particle Hamiltonian of P5
with mass set to zero: the framework's massive family has no massless
self-adjoint member obtained as $m\downarrow0$
([[cex-nrqm-framework-zero-mass-has-no-self-adjoint-limit]]), and no such limit
is used here.

**(ii) Quantised transverse radiation sector.** The model assigns to the free
radiation a **bosonic species** in the sense of P6, whose one-particle space is
the transverse space
$$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3}):\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for almost every }k\Bigr\}$$
with the $L^{2}$ inner product; its $n$-particle sector is
$\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}=\operatorname{ran}P_{+}^{(n)}$ and its radiation state
space is the bosonic Fock space $F(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}$
([[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]]). The
statistics choice "bosonic" is an empirical model assignment of P6 clause (iii)
and is not derived here; it is motivated by the photon's observed
indistinguishability and integer spin but is adopted, not deduced.

**(iii) Mode assignments of frequency, energy and momentum.** In the declared
inertial chart, each free mode label $k\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ is
assigned the **angular frequency** $\omega(k):=c|k|$ in $\mathrm s^{-1}$, the
**photon energy** $E(k):=\hbar\omega(k)=\hbar c|k|$ in joules and the
**photon momentum** $p(k):=\hbar k$ in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$,
where $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}\ \mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ and
$\hbar=h/(2\pi)>0$ in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$ have the SI values of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (c). Ordinary frequency is
$\nu(k)=\omega(k)/(2\pi)$ in hertz. These are separate quantum-radiation model
assignments: they are neither consequences of classical Maxwell theory nor
consequences of the special-relativistic framework, and no Lorentz
transformation law for the mode label $k$, for $\omega(k)$ or for the
polarisation pair is adopted or claimed; the extension does not assert Galilean
covariance of the radiation sector, and it does not identify the massless
Lorentz representations of the photon with the representations of the spatial
rotation group used in P6.

**(iv) Free-field observables.** The model assigns the total free-field energy
observable $H_f=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_{n}$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$ and
$T_{n}\psi=\varepsilon_{n}\psi$, read in joules, the total number observable $N$
read in the dimensionless unit $1$ of counted quanta, and the total momentum
components $\bigoplus_n\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\hbar k_{j,i}\bigr)$, read in
$\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$; their operator domains and
self-adjointness are the mathematics of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
and [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]] for energy and

Let $s\in\frac12\mathbb N=\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$, put $N:=2s\in\mathbb N$ and let
$V_s:=\mathbb C^{N+1}$ carry the standard inner product
$\langle z,w\rangle=\sum_{k=0}^{N}z_k\overline{w_k}$, linear in the first argument
([[def-inner-product-space]]). Write $(e_m)_{-s\le m\le s}$ for the standard basis, indexed so that
$e_m$ is the vector with entry $1$ in position $k=s-m$ and entry $0$ elsewhere; thus
$\langle e_m,e_n\rangle=1$ if $m=n$ and $\langle e_m,e_n\rangle=0$ otherwise. Define $\mathbb C$-linear maps
$J_z,J_+,J_-\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V_s)$ by their values on this basis ([[def-linear-map]]):

$$J_ze_m:=m\,e_m,\qquad J_+e_m:=\sqrt{(s-m)(s+m+1)}\,e_{m+1},\qquad J_-e_m:=\sqrt{(s+m)(s-m+1)}\,e_{m-1},$$

where $e_{s+1}:=0$ and $e_{-s-1}:=0$, and put

$$J_x:=\tfrac12(J_++J_-),\qquad J_y:=\tfrac1{2i}(J_+-J_-),\qquad J^2:=J_x^2+J_y^2+J_z^2 .$$

Then:

(a) $J_z$, $J_x$ and $J_y$ are self-adjoint endomorphisms of $V_s$
([[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]]), and $J_+^*=J_-$, $J_-^*=J_+$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]);

(b) on $V_s$ the commutators are

$$[J_z,J_+]=J_+,\qquad [J_z,J_-]=-J_-,\qquad [J_+,J_-]=2J_z,\qquad [J_x,J_y]=iJ_z,\qquad [J_y,J_z]=iJ_x,\qquad [J_z,J_x]=iJ_y ;$$

(c) $J^2=J_-J_++J_z^2+J_z=J_+J_-+J_z^2-J_z=s(s+1)I$, and $[J^2,J_z]=[J^2,J_\pm]=0$;

(d) the matrix elements of the raising operator are
$\|J_+e_m\|^2=(s-m)(s+m+1)$ and $\|J_-e_m\|^2=(s+m)(s-m+1)$, and
$\langle J_+e_m,e_{m+1}\rangle=\sqrt{(s-m)(s+m+1)}$, which is nonzero exactly when $m<s$;

(e) for $s=\tfrac12$, identify $V_{\frac12}=\mathbb C^2$ with the basis ordered as $(e_{\frac12},e_{-\frac12})$ and let

$$\sigma_x:=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_y:=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\ i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_z:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$$

be the Pauli matrices. Then $J_i=\tfrac12\sigma_i$ for $i=x,y,z$, $\sigma_x^2=\sigma_y^2=\sigma_z^2=I$,
$\sigma_x\sigma_y=i\sigma_z$, $\sigma_y\sigma_z=i\sigma_x$, $\sigma_z\sigma_x=i\sigma_y$, and consequently
$\sigma_i\sigma_j+\sigma_j\sigma_i=2\delta_{ij}I$ and $\sigma_i\sigma_j=\delta_{ij}I+i\sum_k\varepsilon_{ijk}\sigma_k$ for all $i,j$, where $\delta_{ij}=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise, and $\varepsilon_{ijk}$ denotes the sign of the permutation $(x,y,z)\mapsto(i,j,k)$.

All statements are finite-dimensional linear algebra: no physical interpretation of $J_x,J_y,J_z$ as angular momentum, and no measurement postulate, is asserted here.

Adopt the framework data and the declared driven model of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] in the **bounded norm-continuous class** of clause (b)(i): $I=[a,b]$ is the declared compact time interval, $\mathfrak H$ the state space of the declared system, $\hbar>0$, and $H:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is norm-continuous with self-adjoint values, $K:=\sup_{t\in I}\|H(t)\|/\hbar<\infty$. Let $U_{0}(t,s)=I$ and $U_{n+1}(t,s)=\int_{s}^{t}A(r)U_{n}(r,s)\,dr$ with $A(r)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}H(r)$ be the oriented Dyson iterates of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]], and let $U(t,s)=\sum_{n\ge0}U_{n}(t,s)$ be its norm-convergent propagator; for $N\in\mathbb N_{0}$ put $R_{N}(t,s):=U(t,s)-\sum_{n=0}^{N}U_{n}(t,s)$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the latter for the outcome-law reading of P2. Then:

(a) *Well-posedness of the declared model.* The family $U$ is the unique family of bounded operators on $\mathfrak H$ that is jointly norm-continuous on $I\times I$, unitary-valued, satisfies $U(s,s)=I$ and the cocycle $U(t,r)=U(t,s)U(s,r)$, and solves $i\hbar\partial_{t}U(t,s)=H(t)U(t,s)$ together with its second-endpoint equation $i\hbar\partial_{s}U(t,s)=-U(t,s)H(s)$ in operator norm. In particular the model's clause (c)(i) declaration has exactly one solution: the driven model in the bounded norm-continuous class is well posed.

(b) *Truncation budget.* For all $s,t\in I$ and all $N\in\mathbb N_{0}$, with $\tau:=|t-s|$,
$$\bigl\|R_{N}(t,s)\bigr\|\le e^{K\tau}\,\frac{(K\tau)^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \|U(t,s)-I\|\le e^{K\tau}-1 .$$
In particular $\|R_{1}(t,s)\|\le e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{2}/2$ and $\|R_{2}(t,s)\|\le e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{3}/6$.

(c) *Evolved states and outcome laws.* For every preparation $\rho$ specified at time $s$ the operator $\rho(t):=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$ is a preparation of the model with $\operatorname{tr}\rho(t)=1$ for every $t\in I$, and the specification is consistent with the cocycle: evolving first from $s$ to $r$ and then from $r$ to $t$ gives the same preparation. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi(s)$ the vector $\psi(t):=U(t,s)\psi(s)$ is unit and spans a pure preparation for every $t$. For every assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]) and every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$, the number $\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)$ is the model's outcome probability at time $t$.

(d) *Error of the unnormalized truncated quadratic estimate.* Let $\psi(s)$ be a unit vector, put $\psi^{N}(t):=\sum_{n=0}^{N}U_{n}(t,s)\psi(s)$ and let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ bounded. Then for every $t\in I$ and every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\bigl|\mu^{A}_{\psi(t)}(B)-\mu^{A}_{\psi^{N}(t)}(B)\bigr|\le (1+\|\sum_{n=0}^NU_n(t,s)\|)\,\|R_N(t,s)\|\le 2\,e^{K\tau}\frac{(K\tau)^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},$$
where the truncated quantity is the unnormalized quadratic form $\mu^{A}_{\psi^{N}(t)}(B):=\|E_{A}(B)\psi^{N}(t)\|^{2}$ of the truncated vector, whose norm is at most $e^{K\tau}$. It is an approximation to the normalized exact Born law and need not itself be a probability law; for $N=1$ the right side is $2e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{2}$.

(e) *Scope.* The theorem is conditional on the bounded norm-continuous class, on the compactness of $I$ and on $K<\infty$. It asserts no existence or uniqueness statement for unbounded families (which are treated in their own classes), no uniform-in-time approximation, no rate or decay, no measurement or apparatus model, and no comparison with any recorded data.

$$H_{\mathrm c}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\bigl(\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}+\sin(\omega t)\sigma_{y}\bigr)\Bigr),\qquad t\in I=[a,b],$$
read as the model's energy family in the bounded norm-continuous class, with $U_{\mathrm c}(t,s)$ its unique unitary propagator ([[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-bounded-norm-propagator]] clause (a)). Put $\Delta:=\omega_{0}-\omega$, $b:=\sqrt{\Delta^{2}+\Omega_{1}^{2}}$, let $R(t):=\cos(\omega t/2)I+i\sin(\omega t/2)\sigma_{z}$ be the rotating frame of [[lem-nrqm-driven-dynamics-two-level-rotating-frame]] and let $P_{\uparrow},P_{\downarrow}$ be the projections onto $\mathbb Ce_{\uparrow},\mathbb Ce_{\downarrow}$, with populations $p_{\bullet}(t):=\langle P_{\bullet}\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle$ of the evolved vector. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) *Exact rotating-frame reduction.* For every solution $\psi$ of $i\hbar\psi'(t)=H_{\mathrm c}(t)\psi(t)$ the rotating-frame vector $\psi_{R}(t):=R(t)\psi(t)$ satisfies exactly
$$i\hbar\psi_{R}'(t)=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\Delta\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\sigma_{x}\bigr)\psi_{R}(t),$$
with the constant matrix $\frac{\hbar}{2}(\Delta\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\sigma_{x})$; equivalently
$$U_{\mathrm c}(t,s)=R(t)^{*}\,e^{-i(t-s)(\Delta\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\sigma_{x})/2}\,R(s)\qquad(s,t\in I).$$

(b) *Rabi populations.* Let $\psi(s)=e_{\uparrow}$ at time $s$. Then for $\tau:=t-s$
$$p_{\downarrow}(t)=p_{\downarrow}^{R}(\tau)=\Bigl|\bigl\langle e_{\downarrow},e^{-i\tau(\Delta\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\sigma_{x})/2}e_{\uparrow}\bigr\rangle\Bigr|^{2}=\frac{\Omega_{1}^{2}}{b^{2}}\sin^{2}\!\Bigl(\frac{b\tau}{2}\Bigr)\qquad(b>0),$$
and $p_{\uparrow}(t)=1-p_{\downarrow}(t)$; the populations of the rotating-frame vector $\psi_{R}(t)$ are the same numbers.

(c) *Resonance and inversion times.* At resonance $\Delta=0$ one has $p_{\downarrow}(t)=\sin^{2}(\Omega_{1}\tau/2)$; when $\Omega_1\ne0$, the drive inverts the population fully at the **pi-pulse** time $\tau=\pi/|\Omega_{1}|$ and returns it to the initial level at $\tau=2\pi/|\Omega_{1}|$; for $b>0$ the population is exactly periodic in $\tau$ with period $2\pi/b$. For $\Omega_{1}=0$ the populations are constant, $p_{\downarrow}\equiv0$ and $p_{\uparrow}\equiv1$.

(d) *Scope.* The statements are exact for the declared finite model and its declared parameters; the rotating frame is a change of description of the same model and does not change the populations. The theorem asserts no damping or relaxation, no decoherence, no measurement record, no identification of $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1}$ with laboratory fields or of the two levels with a species, and no empirical value.

Adopt the framework data and the declared driven model of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] in the **bounded-control class** of clause (b)(ii): $\mathfrak H$ is the model's state space, $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$, $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values, $v=\sup_{t\in I}\|V(t)\|<\infty$ and $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$; let $U(t,s)$ be the mild propagator and put $K:=v/\hbar$. Let $(\varphi_{j})_{j\in J}$ be an orthonormal family in $D(H_{0})$ with $H_{0}\varphi_{j}=E_{j}\varphi_{j}$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]) — a complete family is not required — and fix labels $i,j\in J$ and $s\le t$ in $I$, with $\tau:=t-s$ and $\Delta:=E_{j}-E_{i}$. Let $A_{ji}(t,s)=e^{iE_j\tau/\hbar}\langle U(t,s)\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle$ be the transition amplitude of clause (e) of the model and define its first-order term
$$A^{(1)}_{ji}(t,s):=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_{s}^{t}e^{i\Delta(r-s)/\hbar}\bigl\langle V(r)\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle\,dr .$$
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) *Exact amplitude with Dyson remainder.* There is a remainder $R_{ji}(t,s)$ with
$$A_{ji}(t,s)=\delta_{ij}+A^{(1)}_{ji}(t,s)+R_{ji}(t,s),\qquad |R_{ji}(t,s)|\le e^{K\tau}\frac{(K\tau)^{2}}{2},$$
and if $\|V(r)-V_{0}(r)\|\le\eta(r)$ for a family $V_{0}$ of self-adjoint bounded operators with integrable scalar coefficient $r\mapsto\langle V_{0}(r)\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle$, then the corresponding first-order amplitude differs from $A^{(1)}_{ji}$ by at most $\frac{1}{\hbar}\int_{s}^{t}\eta(r)\,dr$.

(b) *Sinusoidal control.* Let $W\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ be self-adjoint, $\omega,\vartheta\in\mathbb R$, and suppose $V(r)=W\cos(\omega r+\vartheta)$ for $r\in I$. Put $\vartheta_{0}:=\omega s+\vartheta$ and decompose
$$A^{(1)}_{ji}=a_{+}+a_{-},\qquad a_{\pm}:=-\frac{i}{2\hbar}\bigl\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle e^{\mp i\vartheta_{0}}\,\frac{e^{i(\Delta\mp\hbar\omega)\tau/\hbar}-1}{i(\Delta\mp\hbar\omega)/\hbar},$$
with the convention that the quotient is the limit $\tau$ when $\Delta\mp\hbar\omega=0$. Then the *co-rotating* term $a_{+}$ (the one whose denominator vanishes at $\Delta=\hbar\omega$) satisfies
$$|a_{+}|=\bigl|\bigl\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle\bigr|\,\frac{\bigl|\sin\bigl((\Delta-\hbar\omega)\tau/(2\hbar)\bigr)\bigr|}{|\Delta-\hbar\omega|},\qquad\text{and at }\Delta=\hbar\omega:\quad |a_{+}|=\bigl|\bigl\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle\bigr|\frac{\tau}{2\hbar},$$
and the *counter-rotating* term satisfies $|a_{-}|\le|\langle W\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\rangle|/|\Delta+\hbar\omega|$ whenever $\Delta+\hbar\omega\ne0$.

(c) *Outcome probability.* The model's transition probability is $p_{ji}(t,s)=|A_{ji}(t,s)|^{2}$; with $\varepsilon:=e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{2}/2$ and $A^{(1)}:=A^{(1)}_{ji}$, for distinct labels $i\ne j$
$$\bigl|p_{ji}(t,s)-|A^{(1)}|^{2}\bigr|\le 2|A^{(1)}|\,\varepsilon+\varepsilon^{2},$$
and for $i=j$ the survival probability obeys the analogous bound $\bigl|p_{ii}(t,s)-|1+A^{(1)}|^{2}\bigr|\le(2+2|A^{(1)}|)\varepsilon+\varepsilon^{2}$; in both cases the exact outcome probability is controlled by the first-order term and the explicit Dyson error of clause (a).

(d) *Scope.* The statements are finite-time and conditional on the bounded control and on the orthonormal eigenfamily; the remainder bound grows like $\tau^{2}e^{K\tau}$ and no long-time limit, transition rate, exponential decay, continuum density of states or Fermi golden rule is asserted, and no measured frequency, count or rate is claimed.

$$\frac{d}{dt}\bigl\langle U(t,s)\psi,\varphi\bigr\rangle=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\Bigl[\bigl\langle U(t,s)\psi,H_{0}\varphi\bigr\rangle+\bigl\langle V(t)U(t,s)\psi,\varphi\bigr\rangle\Bigr].$$

complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with completed tensor powers
$H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$, contraction maps
$\Psi_f^{(n)}$, Fock space $F(H)$ and core operators $S_\pm(f)$ on the
finite-particle space $F_0$ as in
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]]. For $f\in H$
define
$$D(A_+(f)):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}(n+1)\bigl\|P_+^{(n+1)}(f\otimes\psi_n)\bigr\|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad (A_+(f)\psi)_n:=\sqrt n\,P_+^{(n)}(f\otimes\psi_{n-1})\ (n\ge1),\ (A_+(f)\psi)_0:=0,$$
$$D(A_-(f)):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}(n+1)\bigl\|\Psi_f^{(n)}(\psi_{n+1})\bigr\|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad (A_-(f)\psi)_n:=\sqrt{n+1}\,\Psi_f^{(n)}(\psi_{n+1}).$$
Put $D_1:=\{\psi\in F(H):\sum_n(n+1)\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$. Then:

(a) $A_+(f)$ and $A_-(f)$ are well-defined linear operators on $F(H)$ with the
displayed domains, and they are the closure and the adjoint of the core operator:
$$A_+(f)=\overline{S_+(f)}=S_-(f)^*,\qquad A_-(f)=S_+(f)^*=\overline{S_-(f)}$$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-densely-defined-closed-and-closable-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]);

(b) both $A_\pm(f)$ are closed, densely defined and satisfy
$A_+(f)^*=A_-(f)$, $A_-(f)^*=A_+(f)$; in particular $F_0\subseteq D_1\subseteq D(A_\pm(f))$;

(c) for every $\psi\in D_1$, $\|A_+(f)\psi\|\le\|f\|\,\|\psi\|_1$ and
$\|A_-(f)\psi\|\le\|f\|\,\|\psi\|_1$, where
$\|\psi\|_1^2=\sum_n(n+1)\|\psi_n\|^2$;

(d) for every $g\in H$ and $\psi\in D_1$ the identity
$$\|A_+(g)\psi\|^2=\|A_-(g)\psi\|^2+\|g\|^2\|\psi\|^2$$
holds.

No boundedness of $A_\pm(f)$ on $F(H)$, no self-adjointness of $A_\pm(f)$, and
no physical interpretation is asserted.

public_supplier_section:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\alpha>0$, let
$\mathfrak h$ be the transverse space and $H_f=\bigoplus_nT_n$ the free
transverse Fock Hamiltonian of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]],
and let $A_\pm(g)$, $g\in\mathfrak h$, be the maximal creation and annihilation
operators on $F(\mathfrak h)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]]. Fix a cutoff
$\Lambda>0$ and vectors $g_1,\dots,g_J\in\mathfrak h$ ($J\ge1$) with
$$\operatorname{supp}g_j\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\}\quad\text{and}\quad \frac{g_j}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h,\qquad \varepsilon(k)=\alpha|k|,$$
and define the symmetric operator
$$\phi(g):=A_-(g)+A_+(g),\qquad D(\phi(g)):=D(H_f).$$
Let $d\ge1$, let $H_a$ be a Hermitian $d\times d$ matrix, and let
$D_1,\dots,D_J$ be Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices with operator norms
$\|D_j\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]). Then:

(a) for every $\Psi\in D(H_f)$,
$$\|A_-(g)\Psi\|^2\le\Bigl\|\frac g{\sqrt\varepsilon}\Bigr\|^2\langle H_f\Psi,\Psi\rangle,\qquad
\|A_+(g)\Psi\|^2=\|A_-(g)\Psi\|^2+\|g\|^2\|\Psi\|^2;$$
in particular $\Psi\in D(A_+(g))\cap D(A_-(g))$ and for every $\eta>0$ there is
a finite $C_\eta$ with
$$\|\phi(g)\Psi\|\le\eta\|H_f\Psi\|+C_\eta\|\Psi\| ;$$

(b) $\phi(g)$ is symmetric on $D(H_f)$ and has $H_f$-bound zero
([[def-relative-boundedness-with-respect-to-an-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]);

(c) the free part $H_0:=H_a\otimes I+I\otimes H_f$ with domain
$C^d\otimes D(H_f)$ is self-adjoint on $\mathbb C^d\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$
([[def-hilbert-space]]); for every $\eta_0\in\mathbb R$ the operator
$$H:=H_0+\eta_0\sum_{j=1}^JD_j\otimes\phi(g_j),\qquad D(H):=C^d\otimes D(H_f),$$
is self-adjoint on $\mathbb C^d\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$ and bounded below
([[thm-kato-rellich]],
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-bounded-fixed-n-operator]] (c)).

The product $D_j\otimes\phi(g_j)$ and the coupling $\eta_0$ carry the dimension
of energy in a physical normalisation; this normalisation is a model choice and
no physical statement about radiation or spontaneous emission is made here.

public_supplier_section:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\mathbb H:=\mathbb C$ with its standard inner product (linear in the first
argument), let $F(\mathbb C)$ be its Fock space as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], let
$e_n\in F(\mathbb C)$ be the unit vector supported in coordinate $n$ (so
$(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is a complete orthonormal family of $F(\mathbb C)$),
let $N$ be the number operator and let $A_\pm(1)$ be the maximal creation and
annihilation operators of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] for the vector
$1\in\mathbb C$. Then:

(a) *oscillator coefficients*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$A_+(1)e_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,e_{n+1},\qquad A_-(1)e_n=\sqrt n\,e_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad A_-(1)e_0=0;$$

(b) *coherent vectors*: for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the series
$$\psi_z:=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\frac{z^n}{\sqrt{n!}}\,e_n$$
converges absolutely in $F(\mathbb C)$
([[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]),
$\|\psi_z\|=1$, $\psi_z\in D(A_-(1))$ with
$$A_-(1)\psi_z=z\,\psi_z,$$
and for all $z,w\in\mathbb C$,
$$\langle\psi_z,\psi_w\rangle=e^{-(|z|^2+|w|^2)/2+\overline z w};$$

(c) *number law*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$\bigl|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle\bigr|^2=e^{-|z|^2}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!},$$
and $\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle|^2=1$.

The numbers in (c) are squared moduli of overlaps of unit vectors; identifying
them with outcome probabilities of a number measurement requires a separately
adopted measurement postulate, and no such physical claim is made here.

public_supplier_section:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\hbar>0$.

**(a) The golden-rule kernel.** For $t>0$ define
$$K_t(x):=\frac1{\hbar^2t}\Bigl|\int_0^te^{ixs/\hbar}\,ds\Bigr|^2,\qquad x\in\mathbb R .$$
Then $K_t$ is continuous, nonnegative and even, and for $x\ne0$
$$K_t(x)=\frac{4\sin^2\bigl(xt/(2\hbar)\bigr)}{x^2t},\qquad K_t(0)=\frac t{\hbar^2};$$
moreover for every $\delta>0$ and every $x$ with $|x|\ge\delta$,
$$K_t(x)\le\frac4{x^2t}\le\frac4{\delta^2t},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}K_t(x)\,dx=\frac{2\pi}{\hbar}.$$

**(b) Approximate identity.** Let $J\in L^1(\mathbb R)$
([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]) and let $\Delta\in\mathbb R$.
If the representative $J$ is continuous at $\Delta$
([[def-continuity-real]]), then
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb R}K_t(x)J(\Delta+x)\,dx=\frac{2\pi}{\hbar}J(\Delta)$$
([[def-limits-at-infinity]]).

**(c) First-order emission coefficient.** Adopt the objects and hypotheses of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]]: $\alpha>0$, the
transverse space $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_\Pi$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
with $\varepsilon(k)=\alpha|k|$, the cutoff $\Lambda>0$, the vectors
$g_1,\dots,g_J\in\mathfrak h$ ($J\ge1$) with
$$\operatorname{supp}g_j\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\},\qquad \frac{g_j}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h,$$
the Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices $H_a,D_1,\dots,D_J$ and the coupling
$\eta_0\in\mathbb R$. Let $v_a,v_b$ be orthonormal eigenvectors of $H_a$ with
$H_av_a=E_av_a$, $H_av_b=E_av_b$, and let $\Delta:=E_a-E_b>0$. Put
$$c_j:=\langle D_jv_a,v_b\rangle\ (\mathbb C^d\text{ inner product}),\qquad M:=\sum_{j=1}^Jc_jg_j\in\mathfrak h,$$
and define the finite Borel measure
$$\nu_b(A):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\mathbf 1_A(\varepsilon(k))\,\|M(k)\|^2\,d^3k, \qquad A\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},$$
and for $t\ge0$ the amplitude
$$A_b(k,t):=-\frac{i\eta_0}{\hbar}M(k)\int_0^te^{i(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta)s/\hbar}\,ds .$$
Then:

(i) $\nu_b$ is a finite Borel measure on $\mathbb R$ with
$\nu_b(\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda])=0$, and
$$\int_{\mathbb R}f\,d\nu_b=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f(\varepsilon(k))\,\|M(k)\|^2\,d^3k$$
for every Borel $f\ge0$;

(ii) $A_b(\cdot,t)\in\mathfrak h$ for every $t\ge0$, and
for $t>0$,
$$\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^2 =\eta_0^2t\int_{\mathbb R}K_t(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_b(E).$$
At $t=0$ the amplitude is zero, so its squared norm is zero; no $K_0$ is used.

(iii) if $\nu_b=J_b\lambda$ for some $J_b\in L^1(\lambda)$ with $J_b=0$
$\lambda$-a.e. on $\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda]$ and the representative $J_b$
continuous at $\Delta$, then for $0<\Delta<\Lambda$
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac1t\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^2 =\frac{2\pi\eta_0^2}{\hbar}J_b(\Delta);$$
if instead $\Delta>\Lambda$, then the same limit exists and equals $0$. The
boundary case $\Delta=\Lambda$ is not asserted.

*Motivation and scope.* In the cutoff dipole model of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]] the vector
$A_b(\cdot,t)$ is the explicit single-vertex amplitude with the atom passing
from $v_a$ to $v_b$ and one photon emitted; $\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|^2$ is the
corresponding first-order photon coefficient, and (iii) is the golden-rule
limit of that coefficient divided by $t$. This item computes only the limit of
the explicit coefficient, under the stated hypotheses on the spectral density
$J_b$. It asserts no approximation of the exact model evolution, no all-time or
weak-coupling limit, no Markov property and no exact exponential decay, and it
reports no measurement or empirical rate. The parameter $\hbar$, the coupling
$\eta_0$ and the matrices $D_j$ enter as mathematical normalisation data of the
model; their physical identification is a separate assumption.

public_supplier_section:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert
space with inner product linear in the first argument
([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Let
$H^{\otimes 0}:=\mathbb C$, $H^{\otimes 1}:=H$ and
$H^{\otimes(n+1)}:=H^{\otimes n}\widehat\otimes H$ be the completed tensor
powers with elementary tensors $u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_n$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]); for $n\ge 1$ let
$P_+^{(n)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$ be the symmetric projection of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] and set
$P_+^{(0)}:=\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb C}$. Write $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ for
its range and define

$$F(H):=\Bigl\{\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}:\ \psi_n\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\ \text{for all }n,\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$$

Then:

(a) for $\psi,\varphi\in F(H)$ the scalar series
$\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\langle\psi_n,\varphi_n\rangle$ converges absolutely and
defines a sesquilinear form, linear in the first argument, with respect to
which $F(H)$ is a complex vector space with inner product
$\langle\psi,\varphi\rangle:=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\langle\psi_n,\varphi_n\rangle$
([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]],
[[def-series-and-absolute-convergence-in-a-normed-space]]);

(b) $(F(H),\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ is a Hilbert space, i.e. the induced norm
is complete ([[def-hilbert-space]]);

(c) the vacuum vector $\Omega:=(1,0,0,\dots)$ satisfies $\|\Omega\|=1$, and the
finite-particle space
$F_0:=\{\psi\in F(H):\psi_n=0\ \text{for all but finitely many }n\}$ is a dense
linear subspace of $F(H)$ ([[def-dense-top]]);

(d) for every $n$ the map
$\iota_n:\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\to F(H)$,
$\iota_n(u):=(0,\dots,0,u,0,\dots)$ (entry in coordinate $n$) is a linear
isometry of $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ onto the closed subspace of vectors
supported in coordinate $n$;

(e) if $H$ admits a countable complete orthonormal family
$(e_i)_{i\in I}$, $I$ at most countable
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
then $F(H)$ is separable ([[def-separable-space]]);

(f) *direct sums of self-adjoint operators*: if for every $n\ge 1$ a self-adjoint
operator $T_n$ on the Hilbert space $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ with domain
$D(T_n)\subseteq\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ is given
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-unbounded-linear-operator-domain-and-graph]]), and

$$D(T):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\ \psi_n\in D(T_n)\ \text{for all }n,\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\|T_n\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad (T\psi)_n:=T_n\psi_n,$$

then $T$ is self-adjoint and $D(T)$ is dense; if in addition every $T_n$ is
bounded with $\sup_{n}\|T_n\|<\infty$, then $T$ is bounded with
$\|T\|=\sup_n\|T_n\|$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).

No physical interpretation of $F(H)$, of the tensor powers or of the direct-sum
operators is asserted.

public_supplier_section:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space with completed tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric
projections $P_+^{(n)}$ and Fock space $F(H)$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]]. Define the
number operator by
$$D(N):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n^2\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad (N\psi)_n:=n\psi_n .$$
Then:

(a) $N$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on $F(H)$ with the displayed
domain; $N\ge0$ in the sense that $\langle N\psi,\psi\rangle\ge0$ for
$\psi\in D(N)$, $N\Omega=0$, and $F_0$ is a core for $N$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]);

(b) for every $n$, every nonzero $u\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ satisfies
$N\iota_n(u)=n\,\iota_n(u)$, and for $H\ne\{0\}$ the spectrum of $N$ is
$\sigma(N)=\mathbb N$;

(c) for $f\in H$ and $\psi\in F_0$ the core operators of
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]] satisfy
$$N S_+(f)\psi-S_+(f)N\psi=S_+(f)\psi,\qquad N S_-(f)\psi-S_-(f)N\psi=-S_-(f)\psi ;$$

(d) $D(N)\subseteq D_1:=\{\psi:\sum_n(n+1)\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$, and for every
$\psi\in D(N)$,
$$\|N\psi\|^2=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n^2\|\psi_n\|^2,\qquad \langle N\psi,\psi\rangle=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n\|\psi_n\|^2 .$$

No physical interpretation of $N$, and no assertion about particle number
measurement, is made.

public_supplier_section:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the Axiom of Dependent Choice and the
Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a parameter $\alpha>0$, define the transverse
subspace
$$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3):\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for a.e. }k\Bigr\}$$
with the $L^2$ inner product, define the bounded multiplier-valued function
$\Pi(k):=\mathrm{id}-|k|^{-2}kk^{\mathsf T}$ for $k\ne0$ and $\Pi(0):=0$, and let
$M_\Pi$ be multiplication by $\Pi$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]). Write
$\varepsilon(k):=\alpha|k|$ and let $M_\varepsilon$ be multiplication by
$\varepsilon$, with $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}:=M_\varepsilon|_{\mathfrak h}$.
Let $F(\mathfrak h)$ be the Fock space of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] with sectors
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$, and for $n\ge1$ define
$$T_n\psi:=\varepsilon_n\psi,\quad \varepsilon_n(k_1,\dots,k_n):=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha|k_i|,\qquad D(T_n):=\{\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}:\varepsilon_n\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\},$$
and $T_0:=0$ on $\mathbb C$. Finally put
$$H_f:=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_n,\qquad D(H_f):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(\mathfrak h):\ \sum_n\|T_n\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$$
Then:

(a) $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_\Pi$ is a closed separable subspace of
$L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$, invariant under $M_\varepsilon$, and
$\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on
$\mathfrak h$ with $D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})=\{f\in\mathfrak h:\varepsilon f\in\mathfrak h\}$
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]],
[[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]);

(b) each $T_n$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on the Hilbert space
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ with the displayed domain
([[def-hilbert-space]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]);

(c) $H_f$ is self-adjoint and positive with domain $D(H_f)$; it commutes with
every sector projection $\Pi_n$ (i.e. $T_n$ maps its sector into itself);

(d) for every $\beta>0$ the bounded operator $e^{-\beta H_f}$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]) is not compact and in particular not trace
class ([[def-compact-linear-operator]], [[def-trace-class-operator]]); more
precisely its restriction to the one-particle sector equals the multiplication
operator $M_{e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}$ on $\mathfrak h$, which is not compact, and
the restriction of a compact operator to a closed invariant subspace is compact.

The identification of $\mathfrak h$, $\varepsilon$ and $H_f$ with physical
transverse photons in a chosen frame is a separate model assumption and is not
asserted here; no thermal interpretation of $e^{-\beta H_f}$ is claimed either.
