Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Adopt the objects and
hypotheses of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]]:
$d\ge1$, Hermitian matrices $H_a,D_1,\dots,D_J$ on $\mathbb C^d$, cutoff
$\Lambda>0$, transverse vectors $g_j$ with
$\operatorname{supp}g_j\subseteq\{0<\varepsilon\le\Lambda\}$ and
$g_j/\sqrt\varepsilon\in\mathfrak h$, coupling $\eta_0\in\mathbb R$,
$$H_0:=H_a\otimes I+I\otimes H_f,\qquad B:=\eta_0\sum_{j=1}^JD_j\otimes\phi(g_j),\qquad H:=H_0+B,$$
all with domain $C^d\otimes D(H_f)$ so that $H_0$ and $H$ are self-adjoint on
that domain. Fix $\hbar>0$, a unit vector $v_a\in\mathbb C^d$ and
$\Psi_0:=v_a\otimes\Omega$, and define the interaction-picture family
$$V(t):=e^{itH_0/\hbar}Be^{-itH_0/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).$$
For $n\ge0$ and $t\ge0$ let
$$\Psi_n(t):=\Bigl(\frac1{i\hbar}\Bigr)^{\!n}\int_{0<t_1<\cdots<t_n<t}V(t_1)\cdots V(t_n)\Psi_0\,dt_1\cdots dt_n$$
(iterated Bochner integral in $C^d\otimes D(H_f)$; $\Psi_0(t):=\Psi_0$). Put
$C:=2\sum_{j=1}^J\|D_j\|\,\|g_j\|/\hbar$ and $C':=C\Lambda$. Then:

(a) for all $n\ge0$ and $t\ge0$,
$$\|\Psi_n(t)\|\le\frac{(|\eta_0|Ct)^n}{\sqrt{n!}};$$

(b) the vectors $\Psi_n(t)$ lie in $C^d\otimes D(H_f)$, the series
$\sum_{n\ge0}\Psi_n(t)$ converges in the graph norm of $H_f$ uniformly for $t$
in compact subsets of $[0,\infty)$, and its sum $\Psi(t)$ satisfies
$$i\hbar\,\partial_t\Psi(t)=V(t)\Psi(t),\qquad \Psi(0)=\Psi_0 ;$$

(c) the Dyson sum solves the actual self-adjoint evolution:
$e^{-itH_0/\hbar}\Psi(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}\Psi_0$ for every $t\ge0$;

(d) explicit tail bound: for $0\le t\le T$ and $N\ge1$,
$$\Bigl\|e^{-itH/\hbar}\Psi_0-e^{-itH_0/\hbar}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\Psi_n(t)\Bigr\|\le\sum_{n\ge N}\frac{(|\eta_0|CT)^n}{\sqrt{n!}} .$$

The convergence is proved for the actual self-adjoint $H$ on the stated domain;
this is not a formal manipulation of divergent series, and no all-time
weak-coupling, Markov or exponential-decay statement is made.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $P_l$ be the Legendre polynomials of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-legendre-rodrigues-equation]], and for $l\in\mathbb N$ and $0\le m\le l$ define the
function $w_{lm}:(-1,1)\to\mathbb R$ by

$$w_{lm}(t):=(-1)^m(1-t^2)^{m/2}\,\frac{d^m}{dt^m}P_l(t),$$

where $(1-t^2)^{1/2}>0$ denotes the nonnegative square root. Let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on
$S^2$ and let the angle coordinates be $\Phi(\theta,\varphi)=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\sin\theta\sin\varphi,\cos\theta)$
([[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]],
[[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]). Then:

(a) each $w_{lm}$ extends continuously to $[-1,1]$, with $w_{lm}(\pm1)=0$ when $m\ge1$, and on $(-1,1)$
it satisfies the associated Legendre equation
$$-\bigl((1-t^2)w_{lm}'\bigr)'+\frac{m^2}{1-t^2}w_{lm}=l(l+1)w_{lm}\qquad(-1<t<1),$$
equivalently $(1-t^2)w_{lm}''-2tw_{lm}'+\Bigl[l(l+1)-\frac{m^2}{1-t^2}\Bigr]w_{lm}=0$;

(b) for fixed $m\ge0$ the functions $w_{lm}$, $l\ge m$, are pairwise orthogonal in $L^2((-1,1),dt)$:
$\int_{-1}^1w_{lm}w_{km}\,dt=0$ for $k\ne l$; moreover $0<\int_{-1}^1w_{lm}^2\,dt<+\infty$;

[[def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator]]);

[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]). Then, for each fixed $m\in\mathbb N$:

(a) for every $l\ge m$ the polynomial $P_l^{(m)}$ has degree $l-m$ and nonzero leading coefficient, and for
every $d\in\mathbb N$ the polynomials $P_m^{(m)},P_{m+1}^{(m)},\dots,P_{m+d}^{(m)}$ form a basis of the space of
polynomial functions of degree at most $d$ on $[-1,1]$;

(b) the family $(w_{lm})_{l\ge m}$ has dense linear span in $L^2$: if $f\in L^2$ satisfies
$\int_{-1}^1f(t)w_{lm}(t)\,dt=0$ for every $l\ge m$, then $f=0$ almost everywhere; consequently the orthogonal
family $(w_{lm})_{l\ge m}$ is complete in $L^2$ and its normalization $(w_{lm}/\|w_{lm}\|_2)_{l\ge m}$ is a
Hilbert basis of $L^2$, so every $f\in L^2$ has
$f=\sum_{l\ge m}\bigl(\int_{-1}^1f\,w_{lm}\,dt\bigr)\|w_{lm}\|_2^{-2}w_{lm}$ with the finite-subset-net
convergence of [[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]];

(c) for every fixed $m$ the orthogonal projection of $L^2$ onto the one-dimensional span of $w_{mm}$ is
$f\mapsto\|w_{mm}\|_2^{-2}\bigl(\int_{-1}^1f\,w_{mm}\,dt\bigr)w_{mm}$, and $w_{mm}(t)=(-1)^m\frac{(2m)!}{2^mm!}(1-t^2)^{m/2}$.
